blocks.text: Co-dominance is inheritance in which both alleles of a gene pair are fully expressed in the heterozygote, without blending and without one masking the other, so the products of both alleles appear together in its phenotype.

The human MN blood group shows co-dominance. It has two alleles: LM, which produces the M antigen, and LN, which produces the N antigen. When both are present both antigens appear on the red blood cells.

blocks.alt: Left panel: a red four-o'clock flower RR crossed with a white one WW gives pink RW flowers; a 2 x 2 Punnett square of RW x RW gives RR, RW, RW and WW, labelled F2: 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white. Right panel: three red blood cells, the first with only square M antigens (LM LM, M group), the second with only triangular N antigens (LN LN, N group) and the third with both (LM LN, MN group).
blocks.caption: The MN cells on the right show co-dominance (original diagram after Figure 18.3).
blocks.long_description: In incomplete dominance neither allele masks the other, so the heterozygote is intermediate: red RR x white WW four-o'clock plants give all pink RW, and RW x RW gives red, pink and white in a 1:2:1 ratio, the same as the genotype ratio. In co-dominance both alleles are fully expressed side by side: in the MN blood group allele LM makes M antigen and LN makes N antigen, and an LM LN person carries both antigens on the red cells, without any blending.

blocks.caption: Incomplete dominance compared with co-dominance
rows: In the heterozygote both genes blend their phenotypic effects.
In the heterozygote both genes fully express their effects.
The heterozygote shows a phenotype intermediate between the two parents.
The heterozygote shows both parental phenotypes at the same time.
Example: flower colour in the Japanese four-o'clock plant.
Examples: the human MN blood group and the human AB blood group.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: The 'L' stands for Landsteiner and Levine, who discovered this system in 1927. It is also called the MNS system, because the genes of the MN group and of the S/s group are linked on the same chromosome.

blocks.prompt: A man is LM LN and his wife is LN LN. What blood groups can their children have, and in what ratio?
blocks.explanation: The father gives LM or LN, the mother only LN: children are LM LN (MN group) or LN LN (N group), 1:1.

items: Co-dominance: both alleles fully expressed (LM LN carries M and N).
Incomplete dominance blends; co-dominance shows both.
